discovery: Experimental discovery of the Higgs boson through the conception and construction of the ATLAS and CMS detectors at the LHC
motivation: The 2013 Prize recognised the theoretical mechanism, but the 2012 observation of the Higgs boson was an experimental achievement of the first rank. It rests on two general-purpose detectors, ATLAS and CMS, conceived in the late 1980s and early 1990s. Peter Jenni was the founding spokesperson of ATLAS and led it through design, construction and commissioning. Michel Della Negra founded CMS and led it as spokesperson, and Tejinder Virdee shaped its crystal electromagnetic calorimeter and later led the collaboration. Their choices gave the precision in photon, lepton and tracking measurement, and the control of systematics, that made the discovery possible in the diphoton and four-lepton channels. More than a decade on, these detectors have established the Higgs couplings to gauge bosons, third-generation fermions and now muons. They are also opening access to Higgs pair production and the self-coupling, which tests the shape of the Higgs potential.
